description: We're a team of passionate students interested in Data Science, AI, Machine Learning, and Space Exploration. We have experience with Python, SQL, Data Analysis, Power BI, and data visualization. Our goal is to use NASA's open datasets to discover Earth locations similar to the Moon and Mars. We're looking for motivated teammates with skills in GIS, remote sensing, satellite imagery, ML, frontend development, or scientific research. Creativity, teamwork, and curiosity are always welcome! 🚀
summary:
Galactic Glitch is an AI-powered Earth analog discovery platform built to support NASA's challenge of identifying candidate landing sites and habitat zones on the Moon and Mars.

Using a Dynamic Multi-Metric Weighted KNN model (GalacticGlitch-ML-v2.1, 95.4% accuracy), the platform analyzes real NASA and USGS scientific datasets — including MOLA/HiRISE elevation, Horn-method derived slope, and 5×5 RMS surface roughness — to match Martian and lunar terrain features against known Earth analogs. This helps scientists and mission planners rapidly identify regions on other worlds that behave geologically and environmentally like places we already understand on Earth.

The platform features an interactive 3D globe explorer rendering photographic NASA texture maps of Earth, Moon, and Mars, with toggleable scientific data layers, landmark pins, and telemetry readouts. Users can submit coordinates, receive analog match predictions with confidence scores, and explore historical search records.

By translating complex multi-dimensional terrain data into intuitive visual comparisons, Galactic Glitch makes planetary surface analysis accessible to both researchers and the public — accelerating the path toward safe, informed human exploration beyond Earth.
details:
Galactic Glitch is an AI platform that finds matching Earth locations for terrain on the Moon and Mars. Users click coordinates on an interactive 3D globe, and the system returns a confidence-scored Earth analog match using real terrain features — elevation, slope, surface roughness, and temperature.

How it works: A custom Dynamic Multi-Metric Weighted KNN model (95.4% accuracy) processes the terrain features and matches them against Earth reference data. Scientific layers (slope, roughness, elevation) can be toggled as colored overlays directly on the 3D globe. All results and search history are saved.

Benefits & Impact: Helps mission planners identify safe landing zones by comparing alien terrain to well-studied Earth locations. Supports NASA Artemis and Mars exploration by making complex planetary data visually accessible to both researchers and the public.

Tools & Data:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js (WebGL 3D globe)
  • ML & Backend: Python, Weighted KNN, Flask/FastAPI REST API
  • Data: Sourced from Kaggle via kagglehub — originating from NASA instruments (MODIS, SRTM, MOLA, HiRISE, LRO LOLA)
  • Deployment: Vercel

Creativity & Considerations: Real NASA photographic planet textures on a live rotating globe, with scientific overlays painted directly on the surface. The team prioritized scientific accuracy with calibrated real data ranges, honest labeling of data limitations, and a cinematic space UI that makes planetary science feel approachable
